answers.question: If the behaviour of `UserService.getUserByUuid` in openmrs-core changed, which code in the REST web services module (openmrs-module-webservices.rest) uses it and could be affected?

paragraphs.text: **Declaration analysed:** the `UserService` interface method `UserService.getUserByUuid(String uuid)` [1], implemented by `UserServiceImpl.getUserByUuid` [2] (delegating to the DAO) and by `HibernateUserDAO.getUserByUuid` [3]. Its contract is: return the user for the uuid, `null` if not found, `APIException` on error, and `AccessDeniedException` if the caller lacks the GET_USERS privilege (enforced by the `@PreAuthorize` on the interface) [4]. Note the separate, same-named `ContextDAO.getUserByUuid` [5] — a name clash, not part of this analysis.

- `UserConverter1_8.getByUniqueId` returns `Context.getUserService().getUserByUuid(string)` [6]. This is the widest blast radius: `ConversionUtil.getConverter(User.class)` finds this handler (it is `@Handler(supports = User.class, order = 0)` [7]), and `ConversionUtil` calls `getByUniqueId` for any String→object conversion [8], and for any incoming map carrying a `uuid` property [9]. So *every* REST payload that supplies a `User` by uuid runs through `getUserByUuid`, not just the user endpoints.
- `UserResource1_8.getByUniqueId` backs `GET /user/{uuid}` [10]. It maps the result to `new UserAndPassword1_8(user)` only when non-null, so a change in the null-return contract changes whether the request 404s or NPEs.
- `ProviderSearchHandler1_9.search` resolves the `user` search parameter, and already branches on `user == null` to return `EmptySearchResult` [11]. This handler is what `GET /provider?user={uuid}` uses [12]; a privilege change here would surface as an error instead of an empty page.
- `AlertRecipientResource2_0.setRecipientProperty` re-looks-up the recipient by uuid and silently skips assignment when the result is null omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs2_0/AlertRecipientResource2_0.java — a null behaviour that would make alert-recipient creates quietly drop the recipient.
- `ChangePasswordController1_8.changeOthersPassword` resolves the target user under a pushed `GET_USERS` proxy privilege omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs1_8/ChangePasswordController1_8.java. It relies on `getUserByUuid` throwing nothing but returning null: null or a null `userId` becomes a 404 via the `NullPointerException` handler omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs1_8/ChangePasswordController1_8.java. A change to throw instead of returning null would bypass that and return a 500.

- `UserResource2_0Test` and `UserResource1_9Test` build fixtures with `new UserAndPassword1_8(Context.getUserService().getUserByUuid(getUuidProperty()))` omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs2_0/UserResource2_0Test.java and omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_9/UserResource1_9Test.java.
- `UserController1_8Test` asserts post-create/edit/retire state through it omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs1_8/UserController1_8Test.java and omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs1_8/UserController1_8Test.java, and asserts search hits against it omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs1_8/UserController1_8Test.java.
- `UserController2_0Test` does the same for v2 omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs2_0/UserController2_0Test.java.
- Alert tests use it for fixtures: `AlertResource2_0Test` omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs2_0/AlertResource2_0Test.java, `AlertController2_0Test` omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs2_0/AlertController2_0Test.java, `AlertRecipientResource2_0Test` omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs2_0/AlertRecipientResource2_0Test.java, `AlertRecipientController2_0Test` omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs2_0/AlertRecipientController2_0Test.java.
- `ChangePasswordController1_8Test` authenticates its target via `service.getUserByUuid(RestTestConstants1_8.USER_UUID)` omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs1_8/ChangePasswordController1_8Test.java.
- `PasswordResetController2_2Test` uses the same call for four fixtures omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs2_2/PasswordResetController2_2Test.java. Note the production `PasswordResetController2_2` itself uses `getUserByUsernameOrEmail` instead omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs2_2/PasswordResetController2_2.java, so it is unaffected.

## Likely affected but not verified here

- Other `Resource`/`Converter` handlers in this module that accept a `User`-typed property by uuid only reach `getUserByUuid` indirectly through `ConversionUtil` omod-common/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/ConversionUtil.java; I did not enumerate every such resource, so the list of endpoints above is the confirmed set, not necessarily the complete set.

- Repositories outside the two named: the O3/React frontends in the picked set consume these REST endpoints over HTTP, so they would feel any contract change, but no TypeScript caller can be traced to a Java method through code search.
- Runtime/Spring effects: `@PreAuthorize` is evaluated by AOP proxies and `UserConverter1_8` is selected by `HandlerUtil.getPreferredHandler` reflection omod-common/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/ConversionUtil.java, so a change in how the privilege check or handler ordering resolves would not show up as a static caller.
- I did not run the tests, so I cannot say which of the test assertions above would actually fail.
- If the behaviour change is confined to `HibernateUserDAO` [3] rather than the service layer, the same callers are affected but the `@Transactional`/privilege semantics would come from the service, not the DAO.
